title: && works as a tiny if
why_it_matters: It's the trick behind 'show this only when that is true'.
explanation: a && b gives back a if it's falsy, otherwise b. That makes it a shortcut for 'if a, then b'. Be careful when the left side can be 0: you'll get 0 back, and in React that 0 shows on screen.
code:
const isLoggedIn = true;
console.log(isLoggedIn && "Welcome back"); // Welcome back
console.log(false && "never seen");        // false
console.log(0 && "never seen");            // 0
try_it: Predict the output of '' && 'hi' before you run it.
